title: 6% Yields By Year-End, 9% Mortgages—Stocks Get ‘Rug Pulled’ | Todd Horowitz
speaker: Todd 'Bubba' Horwitz

macro_themes.view: Strong demand for money and sticky inflation push the 10-year toward 6% by year-end; mortgages could hit 9%.
Real inflation is closer to 10% than the reported ~3.4-3.7%; Fed may hike once or twice more this year.
There is a glut of crude that just isn't refined; Republicans need lower oil before the midterms.
Volume ~50% of normal, no institutional participation; AI is a bubble and a 'rug pull'/major meltdown is coming.
Countries are buying dollars out of fear; the euro could fall below parity.
Rising card delinquencies and auto/mortgage defaults; housing slowing.

calls.condition: Still short; working orders to sell more at 95 if an Iran flare-up pushes oil back into the 90s.
calls.reason: Crude glut that isn't being refined; administration must get oil lower before the midterms; agency bullish forecasts are 'talking their book'.
calls.quote: I'm looking for oil to be below 70 before the year is out... I think we'll probably see 85 before the week is over.

calls.instrument_quoted: US 10-year yield (%); also short 30y (114->102) and 10y (109->104) bond futures
calls.condition: Target 6% by year-end; also sees mortgages possibly reaching 9%. Action 'short' refers to his short bond positions.
calls.reason: Huge demand for money, heavy issuance and sticky inflation; free-market rates should be higher; he called 5% by September.
calls.quote: I think we have a real good shot to get to 6% because there's a A of demand for money

calls.condition: Will not short for a multi-week/month swing until the chart signals a top; an 8,000 S&P first would not surprise him.
calls.reason: Retail-driven grind higher on ~50% normal volume; NQ/ES breaking out while Dow and Russell sit on support; AI bubble and higher rates will 'pull the rug'.
calls.quote: they're about ready to see the rug pulled from underneath them... if we got the 8,000 S&P, it would not surprise me one bit.

calls.condition: Says metals may have 'a little bit more room to go on the downside' first.
calls.reason: Gold's 35% drop already priced in higher rates; inflation still not priced in; held $4,000 despite higher yields and dollar.
calls.quote: I have been buying gold all along here down around the 44100 4200 level... we're now going to start to see that move higher again.

calls.reason: Likes the metals as a place to park money; buying silver at 60.

calls.condition: 100k by year-end only if equity volatility picks up; at the current slow pace, no.
calls.reason: Base around 60k, growing adoption, not controlled by the Fed; currently stuck in an 80-90k range. Has been buying 75-80k.
calls.quote: right now it's stuck in a range between 80 and 90,000... I give you a strong maybe.

calls.instrument_quoted: US dollar index; EUR/USD quoted as '112' (1.12)
calls.condition: Target 104-105 (recorded 105); also says EUR/USD could fall below parity from ~1.12.
calls.reason: Global fear has countries buying dollars; the euro is in trouble and could go below parity; yen intervention failed.
calls.quote: I think the dollar's got a chance to see 104 105 if not higher.

calls.reason: Memory/storage names are overbought and in bubble territory along with AI generally, but he won't fight the trend.
calls.quote: I think they're overbought. I think we're in bubble territory, but you know, look, I'm not going to fight what's going on.

calls.reason: Really likes SpaceX; bought at 113 and added at 150.
calls.quote: I really like SpaceX a lot here... I bought SpaceX at 113, and I bought more at 150.
